title: Tor dimension shifting along two short exact sequences
statement: Let S be a commutative ring, k an S-module, and 0 \to K_1 \to F_0 \to M \to 0 and 0 \to K_2 \to F_1 \to K_1 \to 0 exact sequences with F_0 and F_1 free, with Tor as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Then there is a natural isomorphism Tor_1^S(K_2,k) \cong  Tor_3^S(M,k). In particular, if M has a projective resolution of length at most two, then Tor_1^S(K_2,k)=0.

source.place: proof, dimension shifting after the first two free presentations

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-p1-tor-dimension-shift-natural] to the exact sequence 0 \to K_2 \to F_1 \to K_1 \to 0 (F_1 free) with i=1. It gives isomorphisms Tor_2^S(K_1,N) \cong Tor_1^S(K_2,N), natural in the S-module N; take N=k.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (dimension shifting for the displayed free presentation)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-p1-tor-dimension-shift-natural] to the exact sequence 0 \to K_1 \to F_0 \to M \to 0 (F_0 free) with i=2. It gives isomorphisms Tor_3^S(M,N) \cong Tor_2^S(K_1,N), natural in N. Composing at N=k the isomorphism of Step 1 with the inverse of this one yields an isomorphism Tor_1^S(K_2,k) \cong Tor_3^S(M,k); as a composite of isomorphisms natural in N (the inverse of a natural isomorphism is natural), it is natural in k.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (dimension shifting for the displayed free presentation)

proof.text: If M has a projective resolution of length at most two, choose one concentrated in degrees 0, 1, and 2. By [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], Tor_3^S(M,k) is the third homology of the resolution tensored with k; the degree-3 and degree-4 terms are zero, so this homology vanishes. The isomorphism of Step 2 then gives Tor_1^S(K_2,k)=0.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00LY (definition of Tor by homology of a projective resolution)

proof_origin.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 together with Section Tag 00LY
